## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Targeting GPCRs with protein degraders](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41573-026-00177-4)** — *Nature Reviews Drug Discovery*
  - A review details advances in applying targeted protein degradation (TPD) strategies to G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), expanding degradation approaches beyond intracellular target proteins to membrane-bound receptors.

- **[Synthetic heparin oligosaccharide decouples HIT risk from anticoagulation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42981431/)** — *PubMed*
  - Researchers engineered a synthetic heparin oligosaccharide that retains full anticoagulant potency while eliminating binding to platelet factor 4 (PF4), removing the risk of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT).

- **[CSF PrP-amyloid seeding predicts symptomatic conversion in inherited prion disease](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.03.26367164)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Longitudinal evaluation of 94 *PRNP* E200K mutation carriers demonstrated that real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) positivity in cerebrospinal fluid occurs a median of 2.0 years (IQR 1.3–3.3) before clinical symptom onset.
  - Asymptomatic carriers who maintained negative RT-QuIC results did not convert during follow-up, supporting seeding activity as a short-term predictive biomarker for intervention timing.

- **[Plasma GFAP mediates amyloid-tau progression across the Alzheimer's spectrum](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.03.26366374)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Integrated fluid and PET biomarker analyses across two independent cohorts (n = 278 and n = 236) show plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) statistically mediates the relationship between soluble Aβ₄₂/₄₀ ratios and amyloid PET, as well as between amyloid PET and tau PET accumulation.

- **[Metagenomic profiling reveals opposing gut microbiome axes in chronic disease](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04744-5)** — *Nature Medicine*
  - Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 6,803 adults, validated across 13 independent global cohorts, identified two opposing microbiome-mediated functional axes that link specific lifestyle behaviors to 15 distinct chronic and metabolic diseases.

- **[Gene therapy analysis highlights AAV toxicity and commercial concentration](https://x.com/andrewpannu/status/2117997816836497494)** — *Andrew Pannu on X*
  - A landscape report analyzing 465 clinical gene therapy programs and 33 approved drugs shows commercial value concentrated in Zolgensma and Elevidys, which account for 72% of $3.5B in projected 2025 sales.
  - Systemic high-dose AAV intravenous delivery was linked to 6 of 8 in vivo clinical trial deaths tracked since January 2025; subsequent label narrowings contributed to Elevidys quarterly U.S. sales dropping by more than 50%.
  - Efficacy does not ensure adoption, as demonstrated by Roctavian treating only a fraction of eligible severe hemophilia A patients due to safety warnings and steroid co-medication requirements.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **[Biotech]** **[Durability of AAV gene therapy in Crigler–Najjar syndrome](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2603129)** — *NEJM*
  - Long-term follow-up correspondence reports sustained therapeutic expression and persistent serum bilirubin reduction following adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector-mediated gene transfer in patients with Crigler–Najjar syndrome.

- **[De-escalated anti-PD-1 therapy in early triple-negative breast cancer](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42982408/)** — *PubMed*
  - An updated analysis of the NeoTENNIS trial evaluated event-free survival in patients with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer treated with a platinum-free, de-escalated neoadjuvant regimen incorporating anti-PD-1 therapy.

- **[Immune microenvironment remodeling under regorafenib and nivolumab in gastric cancer](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42981428/)** — *PubMed*
  - Longitudinal profiling of patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving regorafenib, nivolumab, and chemotherapy demonstrated specific structural and transcriptional remodeling within the tumor-immune microenvironment correlated with clinical outcome.

- **[Real-time fMRI neurofeedback for amygdala regulation in major depressive disorder](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.03.26367151)** — *bioRxiv*
  - A parallel-group neuroimaging study (n = 21) evaluated an adaptive real-time fMRI neurofeedback framework using dynamic emotional faces, demonstrating targeted, bidirectional amygdala self-regulation to modulate anhedonia and anxiety.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[BMS advances imzokitug monotherapy trials](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2118026624486830442)** — *Jacob Plieth on X*
  - Bristol Myers Squibb is currently enrolling 1,319 patients across clinical trials evaluating its IL-27 inhibitor imzokitug as monotherapy.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Biotech]** **[Plozasiran reduces severe hypertriglyceridemia and acute pancreatitis risk](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2610014)** — *NEJM*
  - Phase 3 trial data published in NEJM demonstrate that plozasiran, an investigational RNAi therapeutic targeting APOC3, significantly lowered triglyceride levels and reduced the risk of acute pancreatitis in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Repatha demonstrates 20% heart attack risk reduction over statin monotherapy](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/05/repatha-vs-zetia-cholesterol-study-heart-attack-risk/)** — *STAT+*
  - Comparative clinical study data showed Amgen's PCSK9 inhibitor Repatha (evolocumab) reduced heart attack risk by 20% compared to secondary add-on options like Zetia (ezetimibe) in patients requiring additional LDL-cholesterol lowering beyond statins.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[GLP-1 receptor agonists lower mortality and hospitalization in diabetic HFrEF](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.03.26367091)** — *bioRxiv*
  - A matched cohort study of 7,878 patients with type 2 diabetes and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) found that initiation of GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with a statistically significant reduction in the composite risk of heart failure hospitalization or all-cause mortality.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[HHS issues interim enforcement discretion for six 503A compounded peptides](http://sciencebasedmedicine.org/not-approved-not-listed-the-hhs-peptide-proposal/)** — *Science-Based Medicine*
  - HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced an interim policy permitting enforcement discretion for state-licensed pharmacies and physicians compounding six peptides (BPC-157, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, and TB-500) while formal 503A bulk drug substance rulemaking proceeds.

- **[FDA details Pre-IND Expedited Rolling Submission Program](http://www.fda.gov/industry/fda-expedited-investigational-new-drug-ind-pilot-program/expedited-ind-rolling-submission-process-and-program-structure)** — *FDA*
  - FDA published structural guidance on its Expedited IND Pilot Program established under HHS Operation TrialBlazer, enabling eligible sponsors to submit nonclinical drug development modules on a rolling basis to accelerate first-in-human clinical trials while maintaining safety oversight.

- **[FDA moves to modernize topical and transdermal bioequivalence standards](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/advancing-generic-drug-development-modernizing-bioequivalence-approaches-topical-transdermal)** — *FDA*
  - FDA announced a public workshop outlining updated bioequivalence approaches and in vitro characterization methods for generic topical and transdermal drug products.

- **[China restricts investigator-initiated biotech clinical trials](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/05/china-biotech-restrictions-impact-rare-disease-investigator-initiated-trial/)** — *STAT+*
  - Chinese regulatory bodies have restricted investigator-initiated trials (IITs) following safety incidents and patient deaths, slowing early-stage rare disease studies and foreign investment access.

- **[India proposes strict drug quality control and automatic license suspension](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/05/india-new-manufacturing-rules-china-clinical-trials/)** — *STAT+*
  - India proposed rules requiring regulatory authorities to immediately suspend drug manufacturing licenses if product batches fail quality standards in government laboratory testing.

- **[FDA schedules guidance webinars on drug interactions and QTc labeling](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/communicating-drug-interaction-and-qtc-information-us-prescribing-information-09232026)** — *FDA*
  - The agency announced a two-part educational webinar focused on draft guidance for communicating drug interaction data and guidance for incorporating QTc prolongation risk into U.S. prescribing information.

- **[FDA holds workshop on Model-Integrated Evidence for generic drugs](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/advancing-generic-drug-development-leveraging-model-integrated-evidence-mie-development-approval)** — *FDA*
  - A half-day regulatory workshop will focus on leveraging Model-Integrated Evidence—including computational modeling and simulation—to support generic drug development and regulatory approval decisions.

- **[FDA publishes pediatric study reviews under BPCA and PREA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-resources/reviews-pediatric-studies-conducted-under-bpca-and-pediatric-assessments-conducted-under-prea-2012)** — *FDA*
  - The agency updated its public repository of medical, statistical, and clinical pharmacology reviews for pediatric assessments conducted under the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act and Pediatric Research Equity Act from 2012 to present.

- **[FDA issues warning letter to Pritam International](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/pritam-international-private-limited-738079-10272026)** — *FDA*
  - The agency issued a warning letter citing Current Good Manufacturing Practice violations and finished pharmaceutical adulteration at Pritam International Private Limited.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Sanofi terminates Nurix-partnered STAT6 degrader program](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/sanofi-discontinue-development-nurix-stat6-degrader-eczema/873697/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Sanofi discontinued development of the co-developed STAT6 targeted protein degrader (NX-0479/SAR444656) for eczema, prompting a drop in Nurix shares and raising technical questions around STAT6 target feasibility.

- **[Big Pharma]** **[Novo Nordisk oral Wegovy sales top Q3 expectations](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novo-wegovy-pill-sales-3q-2026-earnings-cfo/873693/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Novo Nordisk reported third-quarter revenue figures above analyst expectations, driven by early commercial performance of its oral semaglutide formulation.

- **[Biotech]** **[Revolution Medicines reports strong commercial launch for Rasonque](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/05/rasonque-revolution-medicines-pancreatic-cancer-commercial-launch/)** — *STAT+*
  - Revolution Medicines generated record initial uptake and commercial revenues for its newly launched RAS inhibitor, Rasonque, in pancreatic cancer.

- **[Biotech]** **[T-Therapeutics secures $133M Series B for bispecific T-cell engagers](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/t-therapeutics-series-b-tces-bispecifics-cancer-autoimmune/873786/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - T-Therapeutics closed a $133 million Series B financing to advance its T-cell receptor (TCR) engager platform toward undruggable oncology targets and selective autoimmune diseases.

- **[Biotech]** **[Alethio Therapeutics launches with $90M Series A for blood cancers](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/alethio-therapeutics-myeloproliferative-neoplasms-series-a/873775/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Alethio Therapeutics launched with $90 million in Series A funding to develop targeted small molecules for myeloproliferative neoplasms.

- **[Biotech]** **[Ultragenyx slashes 20% of workforce following dual trial failures](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/04/biotech-news-ultragenyx-cuts-staff-after-another-study-fails/)** — *STAT+*
  - Ultragenyx announced it will reduce headcount by approximately 20% and discontinue two clinical-stage rare disease programs after late-stage study readouts failed to hit key endpoints.

- **[CVS Health initiates corporate split separating retail from PBM and insurance divisions](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/cvs-split-two-companies-strategic-about-face/873742/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - CVS Health plans to split into two public entities, uncoupling its retail pharmacy operations from its Caremark PBM and Aetna insurance divisions.

- **[Biotech]** **[ANI Pharmaceuticals offers to acquire Egetis Therapeutics for $560M](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2118284950239908247)** — *BioStocks on X*
  - ANI Pharmaceuticals proposed an offer to acquire Egetis Therapeutics for $560M, with the Egetis Board of Directors unanimously recommending shareholders accept the offer.
  - Concurrently, Egetis announced an agreement to sell a Priority Review Voucher for $190M.

- **[Biotech]** **[Iovance reports $102M Q3 Amtagvi revenue and extends cash runway to 2029](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2118313158146183237)** — *BioStocks on X*
  - U.S. revenue for Amtagvi (lifileucel) reached $102M (up 77% YoY), keeping the company on track to hit its full-year product revenue guidance of $410M to $420M in 2026.
  - Cash reserves of ~$382M are projected to fund operations into 2029.

- **[Biotech]** **[BeiGene reports $1.4B Q3 global sales for Brukinsa](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2118299628164755780)** — *BioStocks on X*
  - Global quarterly revenue for BTK inhibitor Brukinsa (zanubrutinib) reached $1.4B, representing a 34% year-over-year increase.

## Public Health & Policy

- **[US Midterm results set stage for Senate HELP leadership shift and FDA oversight](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/04/bernie-sanders-senate-help-key-role-pdufa-reauthorization/)** — *STAT+*
  - Midterm election outcomes position Sen. Bernie Sanders to lead the Senate HELP Committee, setting up heightened scrutiny around PDUFA reauthorization and pharmaceutical drug pricing controls.

- **[Genomic study tracks post-pandemic evolution and spread of RSV](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.02.26367099)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Global genomic analysis showed post-pandemic RSV circulation was marked by diversity bottlenecks followed by the expansion of novel RSV-A (A.D.3, A.D.5.2) and RSV-B (B.D.E.1) genotypes exhibiting positive selection across the F and G proteins.

- **[Phylogeographic analysis pinpoints origin of cruise ship Andes virus outbreak](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.04.26366130)** — *bioRxiv*
  - Whole-genome sequencing of Andes virus isolates from an outbreak on the *MV Hondius* (12 cases, 3 deaths) traced the index patient's geographic origin of infection to the Tolten-Lanco area in southern Chile.

- **[CMS delays remote patient monitoring rule updates](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/05/health-tech-news-medicare-delays-controversial-rpm-rule-update/)** — *STAT+*
  - Medicare finalized a policy delay on remote patient monitoring (RPM) rules while confirming restrictions that prevent health systems from contracting out RPM services to third-party vendors.

- **[FDA consolidates extended-use date list to address drug shortages](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-shortages/search-list-extended-use-dates-assist-drug-shortages)** — *FDA*
  - The agency updated and consolidated shelf-life extension data for essential drug products to assist healthcare facilities during ongoing drug supply shortages.

- **[FDA expands initiatives for Opioid Use Disorder and overdose reversal](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/postmarket-drug-safety-information-patients-and-providers/opioid-overdose-reversal-medications)** — *FDA*
  - Under the FDA Overdose Prevention Framework, the agency is promoting treatment access for Medications for Opioid Use Disorder and supporting the development and availability of overdose reversal agents, including naloxone and nalmefene.

**Worth watching:** Fall-out from Sanofi's STAT6 degrader failure on the broader targeted protein degradation field, implementation details of the FDA Expedited IND Pilot Program under Operation TrialBlazer, and regulatory developments around HHS's enforcement discretion policy on compounded peptides.

- Biology & Health
    - [FDA approved Arthritis Drug shown to Stop Aggressive Cancer!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JnibEfnCLB4) -- Physionic
        - The video examines how SMARCD1 (a subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex) deficiency drives clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression through mitochondrial reprogramming.
        - It highlights findings showing that mitochondrial complex I activity plays a key functional role in driving kidney cancer metastasis.
        - The content explores repurposing FDA-approved arthritis therapeutics to target altered mitochondrial and metabolic pathways to inhibit aggressive cancer growth.
    - [Understanding reps in reserve | Jeff Cavaliere, M.S.P.T., C.S.C.S.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e1RoRmKWsEE) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Jeff Cavaliere and Peter Attia detail the application of reps in reserve to eliminate "junk volume" and distinguish productive stimulation from unnecessary fatigue.
        - The discussion outlines active rehabilitation strategies for training around partial labrum and rotator cuff tears, noting that total rest slows tissue recovery.
        - It emphasizes prioritizing smaller stabilizing muscles, glutes, and calves, while adapting volume based on midlife recovery signals like joint soreness and systemic fatigue.
    - [Investors Are No Longer Taking Chances](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/DD8_P7aXatg) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Stephanie Davis outlines current capital allocation shifts in the digital health and healthcare AI sectors.
        - Venture capital investors are concentrating funding into a small group of established companies with proven market traction.
        - Early-stage contenders and unverified startups face diminished capital access as investors prioritize risk mitigation over speculative bets.
    - [Founders: Stop Building and Start Talking](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/EFe7IBXFp_o) -- Health2Tech
        - Alison Curfman advises early-stage healthtech founders to pause product development in favor of upfront customer discovery.
        - The video stresses validating core assumptions directly with target users, institutional buyers, and prospective investors before committing engineering resources.
        - Direct engagement helps founders confirm genuine market demand and establish product-market fit before building full-scale solutions.
- Pure Science
    - [The Closest Thing We’ve Got To Real Perpetual Motion](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KfODG5REyss) -- Veritasium
        - The video details the physics and historical milestone of helium liquefaction by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes, explaining why quantum zero-point energy prevents helium from freezing at ambient pressure near absolute zero.
        - It explains superfluidity, Bose-Einstein condensates, Lev Landau's quantum theory of phonons and rotons, and macroscopic quantum effects such as the light-powered fountain effect.
        - The historical narrative highlights Pyotr Kapitsa's experimental discovery of zero viscosity in liquid helium-4 and his intervention to free Lev Landau from prison to formulate the theoretical framework of superfluidity.
- Tech & Engineering
    - [Il traque les parieurs qui ne perdent jamais](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TMRT1mObK8U) -- Underscore_
        - The video addresses how blockchain analysis can be used to track and unmask insider traders and cheaters.
        - The episode features a commercial sponsorship for Incogni, offering a 60% discount on annual subscriptions with the promo code UNDERSCORE.
        - Hosted on set by Matthieu Lambda and Nicolas Vaiman, the audio version of the content is distributed across platforms including Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and Deezer.
- To watch
    - [30 years that shook AI.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/g1eqYBr5qNM) -- Welch Labs
